```{r}
library(regcompR)
families("ordinal")
```

## Cumulative link models

An ordered factor response with a cumulative family gives the proportional
odds model (logit), the ordered probit, and the cloglog, loglog and cauchit
variants. The thresholds are estimated on their natural scale; the main
formula has no intercept.

```{r}
n <- 400
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
d$g <- factor(rep(1:40, each = 10))
d$y <- cut(0.8 * d$x - 0.5 * d$z + rnorm(40, 0, 0.7)[d$g] + rlogis(n), c(-Inf, -1, 0.5, 2, Inf),
           labels = c("low", "mid", "high", "top"), ordered_result = TRUE)
fit <- regcomp(y ~ x + z, family = "cumulative_logit", data = d)
summary(fit)
```

The estimates and standard errors equal those of `MASS::polr()`. A formula
for `scale` gives the location scale model of `ordinal::clm()`:

```{r}
fit_ls <- regcomp(y ~ x + z, scale ~ x, family = "cumulative_logit", data = d)
AIC(fit, fit_ls)
```

Category probabilities:

```{r}
predict(fit, data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1), z = 0), type = "probability")
plot(fit, which = "effects", variable = "x")
```

Continuation ratio (`continuation_ratio_logit`, `_probit`, `_cloglog`),
adjacent category (`adjacent_category_logit`) and stereotype models are also
available, and random effects work as for any other family:

```{r}
fit_m <- regcomp(y ~ x + z + (1 | g), family = "cumulative_logit", data = d)
exp(fit_m$theta)   # random intercept standard deviation (true value 0.7)
```

## Nominal responses

`multinomial_logit` fits the baseline category logit model of
`nnet::multinom()`; the main formula is shared by every non-baseline
category.

```{r}
d$k <- factor(sample(c("a", "b", "c"), n, TRUE, prob = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2)))
fm <- regcomp(k ~ x, family = "multinomial_logit", data = d)
coef(fm)
```

## Bivariate binary responses and selection

`bivariate_binary_odds_ratio` models two binary outcomes with an odds ratio
regression (as in VGAM's `binom2.or`), and `heckman_selection` fits the
sample selection model with response `cbind(selected, outcome)`.
